An embryo ( / ˈ ɛ m b r i oʊ / EM -bree-oh ) is the initial stage of development for a multicellular organism . In organisms that reproduce sexually , embryonic development is the part of the life cycle that begins just after fertilization of the female egg cell by the male sperm cell . The resulting fusion of these two cells produces a single-celled zygote that undergoes many cell divisions that produce cells known as blastomeres . The blastomeres are arranged as a solid ball that when reaching a certain size, called a morula , takes in fluid to create a cavity called a blastocoel . The structure is then termed a blastula , or a blastocyst in mammals .
